2609.31603.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
2609.31603.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) implicitly infer attributes of their users and adapt their behavior accordingly, yet these beliefs remain difficult to inspect and causally manipulate. We introduce Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a unified read-write framework that bridges linear and causal probing by learning a compact user representation that can be both decoded and written back into the model. The frozen LLM acts as its own teacher, distilling beliefs from natural conversations without external annotations. Unlike conventional probing, BSD isolates not only information present in activations, but a state whose causal role can be directly tested. Across multiple model families, BSD faithfully recovers user beliefs and enables substantially stronger interventions than matched hidden-state steering. Crucially, we find that refusal depends not only on the request, but on the model's inferred user intent: changing this belief alters refusal while holding the request fixed. We further uncover a striking cross-model regularity: independently trained LLMs converge on a shared geometry for representing their users. Together, these results reveal implicit user models as readable and causally writable internal states with direct implications for AI safety, shaping how models condition safety decisions on whom they believe they are interacting with.
2609.31603.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）隱性地推斷其用戶的屬性並相應地調整其行為，但這些信念仍然難以檢查和因果操控。<lb/>我們引入了信念自蒸餾（BSD），這是一個統一的讀寫框架，通過學習一個緊湊的用戶表示來橋接線性和因果探測，該表示可以被解碼並寫回模型中。<lb/>凍結的LLM充當其自己的教師，從自然對話中提煉信念，而無需外部註釋。<lb/>與傳統的探測不同，BSD不僅隔離激活中存在的信息，還隔離一種因果角色可以直接測試的狀態。<lb/>在多個模型家族中，BSD忠實地恢復用戶信念，並使得干預的效果顯著強於匹配的隱藏狀態引導。<lb/>關鍵的是，我們發現拒絕不僅取決於請求，還取決於模型推斷的用戶意圖：改變這一信念會在固定請求的情況下改變拒絕。<lb/>我們進一步發現了一個驚人的跨模型規律：獨立訓練的LLMs在表示其用戶時趨向於共享幾何結構。<lb/>綜合這些結果顯示，隱性的用戶模型作為可讀和可因果寫入的內部狀態，對AI安全具有直接的影響，塑造了模型如何根據他們認為正在互動的對象來決定安全決策。
